Advertise UMIP as emulated if and only if the host doesn't natively
support UMIP
column2: otherwise vmx_umip_emulated() is misleading when the host

column1: _does_ support UMIP.  Of the four users of vmx_umip_emulated()
already check for native support
column2: and the logic in vmx_set_cpu_caps() is

column1: relevant if and only if UMIP isn't natively supported as UMIP is set in
KVM's caps by kvm_set_cpu_caps() when UMIP is present in hardware.
That leaves KVM's stuffing of X86_CR4_UMIP into the default cr4_fixed1
value enumerated for nested VMX.  In that case
host support is actually a bug fix of sorts
based solely on descriptor table exiting works only because KVM doesn't
sanity check MSR_IA32_VMX_CR4_FIXED1.  E.g. if a (very theoretical) host
supported UMIP in hardware but didn't allow UMIP+VMX
UMIP but not actually emulate UMIP.  Of course
before it could run a nested VM on said theoretical CPU
modify host CR4 when enabling VMX
column2: i.e. would load an ""illegal"" value into

column1: vmcs.HOST_CR4.
